ersatz

ER-zahts · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ersatz is inferiorly artificial or not genuine; a substitute used out of necessity.

The struggling restaurant served an ersatz crab cake made almost entirely of imitation seafood.

Example

During the shortage, factories produced ersatz rubber from synthetic materials that never performed quite as well as the real thing.

Ersatz specifically describes a substitute created out of necessity, understood by everyone to be inferior to the genuine article.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

imitation: An imitation copies the look or flavor of the real thing — imitation vanilla, imitation leather — and it can do its job perfectly well. Ersatz says more: an ersatz product stands in only because the genuine article cannot be had, and everyone understands it falls short of the original.

synthetic: Synthetic tells you how a thing was made — by chemical processes rather than taken from nature — and passes no judgment on quality; synthetic fabrics often outperform natural ones. Ersatz is all judgment: a substitute used out of necessity and understood to be worse than the real thing.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

genuine: truly what it is said to be

authentic: of undisputed origin; genuine

Where it sits · how far from the genuine article — fake → ersatz → counterfeit

fake vs. ersatz: Fake is a general, everyday word for something not real; ersatz specifically implies an inferior substitute used out of necessity.

counterfeit vs. ersatz: Counterfeit goes further than ersatz, implying an intentional, often illegal attempt to pass a fake off as the real, valuable original.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Ersatz is borrowed whole from German, where it literally means 'replacement' or 'substitute' -- it isn't built from a Latin or Greek root and suffix pair like most of this unit's other words.

Where it comes from

Where it comes from: Ersatz skipped the root-plus-suffix assembly line entirely: English lifted the whole word straight from modern German, where it means 'replacement' or 'substitute.' That is why there are no pieces to break apart and no root relative to hunt for.
